The Organization

At USAFacts, we believe facts deserve to be heard. We turn data from thousands of jurisdictions into clear, unbiased answers about how government spends money and what it achieves. No political agenda. No commercial motive. Just public service.

Founded and funded by Steve Ballmer, former CEO of Microsoft, we work alongside Ballmer Group Philanthropy and Rainier Climate on civic impact.

As an intern, you’ll join a collaborative, mission-driven team and learn how complex public data becomes something the American people can actually use.

To top it off, Fast Company has recognized USAFacts four years running, including the 2026 Most Innovative Companies list. Learn more at usafacts.org and LinkedIn. Learn more about us at usafacts.org and linkedin.com/company/usafacts.

We’d love for you to bring your curiosity, and your conviction that facts matter, to your summer with us.

Your Internship with USAFacts

This is a paid, full-time summer internship for your penultimate year of undergraduate study, where you’ll do real work on real products. Here’s what to expect:

Pay

$33 per hour for at least 10 weeks, which comes to roughly $13,200 before taxes at 40 hours per week. Interns are overtime eligible, so hours over 40 per week are paid at time and a half.

Housing support

Relocating interns receive company-paid furnished corporate housing and a $1,000 travel reimbursement. Interns who live in the area and don’t need corporate housing can be reimbursed up to $2,000 per month for housing costs with a current rental agreement.

Paid sick days and holidays

3 paid sick days and paid holidays for the duration of your internship.

Hybrid schedule

In the office Tuesday through Thursday, with lunches provided, and the flexibility to work remotely or in-office the rest of the week.

Transportation

You’ll receive either an ORCA card for local public transit or paid parking in or near the building.

Events, community, and opportunities

At USAFacts, we believe a great internship is about more than just the work. Throughout the summer, you'll have opportunities to connect with your fellow interns, build relationships across the organization, and make the most of your time in the Seattle area. From organization-wide events and team outings to boat rides, paddleboarding adventures, and sushi dinners, you'll have plenty of opportunities to build connections and have fun along the way. Each intern cohort receives a dedicated morale budget to plan activities together and make the summer their own. You'll also have the unique opportunity to present your projects and accomplishments directly to USAFacts founder and former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer and other organizational leaders.

The Opportunity

At USAFacts, we’re on a mission to provide a comprehensive, unbiased look at our country by the numbers, and our data platform is the foundation that makes it possible.

We’re looking for an aspiring technical product manager who is passionate about data and AI to join our data platform team, which includes data engineers and analysts, data transformation and AI specialists, and technical product managers. You’ll help us build an AI-ready data platform that will power all our ambitions, working alongside our product and engineering teams to build capabilities to acquire, integrate, and analyze government data and make sure it is accurate, complete, and consistent.

This internship is a chance to grow your data and product skills and work with a collaborative team dedicated to making reliable information about the country more accessible to everyone.

Key Priorities and Responsibilities

- Technical Requirements: Help identify and develop technical requirements to optimize the data acquisition experience and increase scalability through AI.

- Feature Ideation: Contribute ideas for new features and improvements based on user feedback, prototyping, experimentation, research, and team collaboration.

- Collaboration: Work closely with design, engineering, and other teams to ensure smooth development and launch of features.

- Product Requirements: Aid in documenting product requirements by collaborating with stakeholders, ensuring clarity and alignment with desired outcomes.

- Assist with Product Roadmap: Support in maintaining and updating the product roadmap for data acquisition and metadata definition of federal, state, and local data, ensuring it aligns with the team’s goals and objectives.

- Workstream Automation: Support in building tools and processes via AI and other means to enable organizational scale and reduce manual interventions.

- Data Quality: Help surface data quality issues and assist in specifying QA plans and use cases to ensure data is accurate, complete, and consistent before it is published.

- Metrics and Analysis: Support in tracking product metrics and KPIs, and analyzing usage and data quality to understand platform performance and areas of improvement.

- Participate in Team Meetings: Attend regular team meetings, product reviews, and other relevant sessions, contributing actively and learning from experienced team members.

The Ideal Candidate

- Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in data science, economics, business, computer science, human-computer interaction, or related technical degree.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills (Python and SQL experience required).

- Interest in building new digital products with a team of PMs, user-experience designers, software engineers, data scientists, and subject matter experts.

- Following the latest developments in the fast-moving AI & LLM space, including technical innovations, design trends, and business impact.

- Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written.

- Ability to work collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Eagerness to learn and adapt in a dynamic work setting.

- Proficient in Microsoft Office or equivalent tools.

- A genuine interest in creating great data products, product management and user experience.

- A genuine interest in civic tech and the power of data in driving positive societal change.

- Experience working on data integration or transformation project preferred.

Additional Information

The position is based in Bellevue, Washington and our organization practices intentional hybrid work​. All USAFacts employees are expected to work on-site Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Mondays and Fridays remain flexible work-from-home or office workdays.

This intern position is a not-exempt role located in Bellevue, WA. The intern role is paid at a rate of $33 per hour. Interns are not eligible for the company’s standard benefits package, but you will receive the paid time off, housing support, and transportation support described above. Start and end dates are flexible between May and September to fit your school schedule, for a minimum of 10 weeks. We’re not able to coordinate academic credit through your school.

Nonpartisan Commitment

USAFacts is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization dedicated to making government data accessible and understandable as a free public service. Consistent with our Political Activity Policy, and to preserve the trust and neutrality essential to our mission, all employees must refrain from political activity that could compromise our impartiality. This includes making political donations, volunteering for or publicly supporting political candidates, parties, or campaigns. Additionally, employees are expected to avoid expressing partisan views on public platforms where they are identifiable as affiliated with USAFacts. This policy helps ensure our work—and our organization—remains trusted, fact-based, and free from political influence.

USAFacts is an equal-opportunity employer and is dedicated to building an inclusive workforce where diversity is valued. Individuals seeking employment at USAFacts are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, martial status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, or sexual orientation.

Navi captures everything a pilot sees and hears and turns it into automated debrief intelligence — sortie-level awareness that has never existed before. None of it works without the hardware in the aircraft. That's what you'll build.

About the role

This is a hands-on hardware internship. You'll build, test, and ship the devices that fly in real aircraft at university flight schools and military squadrons. Every unit you assemble ends up in a cockpit, capturing data a pilot and instructor will sit down and review that same day. Nothing here is a prototype exercise. Navi is already live at leading flight schools.

You'll work directly with our hardware and engineering teams, and you'll see the consequences of your work fast — if a unit fails, you'll hear about it, and you'll be part of fixing it.

What you'll do

- Assemble, wire, and bench-test Navi devices — audio capture, mounting hardware, cable harnesses, enclosures

- Diagnose failures on returned or field-reported units and feed what you learn back into the build

- Help improve the build itself — fixturing, assembly documentation, anything that makes the next hundred units faster and more reliable than the last hundred

- Track inventory, components, and BOMs so we never stall a deployment waiting on a part

- Assist in preparing shipments, and willing to learn and assist in other tasks too

- Work alongside engineers across hardware, firmware, and software to close the loop between what we build and what pilots actually experience

About you

- Currently pursuing a degree in engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience — we care more about what you've built than where you're enrolled

- Comfortable with hand tools, wiring and basic electronics debugging

- Careful and consistent. Hardware that flies has to be built the same way every time, and you take that seriously

- You've built physical things — personal projects, robotics teams, Formula SAE, RC aircraft, drones, a workshop in your garage. Tell us about them

- Willing to do the unglamorous work. Some days are assembly and testing, and those units still have to be perfect

- Curious about why things fail and persistent enough to find out

- Comfortable in ambiguity — processes here are still being written, and you'll help write them

Nice to have

- You know how to fly. A private pilot certificate, student pilot time, or any flight training is a real bonus. Pilots understand the cockpit environment these devices live in, and we'll lean on you for more than device build — flight testing, data collection, ride-alongs, and translating what actually happens in the aircraft back to the engineering team

- Familiarity with aviation systems, avionics, or general aviation aircraft

- CAD, 3D printing, or fabrication experience

- Basic scripting for test automation or data validation

Why this role matters

Pilots trust their lives to the systems in front of them. The device you build is the first link in that chain — if it doesn't capture clean data, nothing downstream works. Interns here own real units going to real customers, not side projects.

What you'll get

- Hardware that ships — your work flies in aircraft at flight schools, airlines, and the U.S. Air Force

- Direct access to the founding team and every part of the stack, from hardware to AI

- A path to a full-time role for interns who prove they can own the build

How we work

- Find a way. We don't wait for permission or perfect information. Ideas come from anywhere regardless of title. Figure it out, ship it, iterate.

- Creativity over control. First principles over process. We'd rather have a creative solution that's 80% right today than a perfect one next quarter.

- Update fast. Come in with a hypothesis, throw it away when the data says otherwise. Ego has no place here.

- Intensity with focus. We work hard because the mission demands it. Clarity on what matters is how we make that sustainable.

About Formlabs:

A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

Your Impact:

As a Print Production Intern on our Sales Enablement Team, you will support our showroom and print production initiatives, including printer maintenance, SLA and SLS print production, and print farm clean-up and logistics to ensure a safe and inspiring environment to produce 3D printed solutions.

Internship Term: Winter/Spring 2027 (January 11 - April 30)
Commitment: Full-time (40 hours/week)
Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA (in-person)

The Job

- Support on design modifications, part layout and slicing for 3D print optimization.

- Support 3D print production including printing, troubleshooting and maintenance across SLA and SLS printers and all Formlabs materials.

- Post process, sand and finish parts.

- Support the team in space maintenance to ensure top of the line health and safety in the showroom and production spaces.

- Create and identify opportunities for space improvements to optimize production, printer utilization, quality control measures, and maintenance while ensuring health and safety of the space and everyone who uses it.

You

- Enjoy working independently.

- Are highly organized and interested in helping streamline processes.

- Have 3D printing experience and are motivated to become a 3D printing expert.

- Are Able to lift 40-80 lbs.

- Are eager to plug into the needs of the Sales team and the Formlabs community.

- Are confident working in Excel/Google Sheets and have a knack for Project Management.

Intern Benefits & Perks:

- Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it

- Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

- Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats

- Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns

- Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

- And of course… unlimited 3D prints

You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here. Please give them a read.

Interns at Formlabs are paid on a bi-weekly pay schedule. The pay range for this role will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. This is a salaried role, so you will always be paid based on the assumed 40 hours per week as a full-time intern. This position does not offer housing or relocation assistance.

$1,000—$1,150 USD

Role Overview

Astera Labs is seeking a Data Analytics Engineer Intern to support reporting, automation, and data pipeline initiatives across the business. This role will help turn business data into actionable insights, scalable datasets, and automated workflows that improve decision-making and operational efficiency.

The ideal candidate brings a strong analytical mindset, curiosity about business systems and data flows, and hands-on experience or coursework in tools such as Excel, Power BI, SQL, and Azure-based data platforms. This person should be comfortable working across both analytics and engineering tasks, partnering with business stakeholders and technical team members to build practical, high-impact solutions.

In this role, you will work primarily with the Business Intelligence team to support reporting, analysis, and automation initiatives in a structured learning environment. Your day may include working with sample or curated datasets, building Excel-based models or trackers, developing Power BI dashboards, writing SQL queries, and assisting with data pipeline and workflow automation tasks. You may also support recurring reporting processes, help document business rules and reporting logic, investigate data quality patterns in non-production datasets, and contribute to lightweight Azure-based integrations and process improvements.

This is a hands-on internship where you will gain exposure to both business intelligence and data engineering work. You will learn how data moves across systems, how dashboards and reports are built for business users, and how automation can improve speed, accuracy, and scalability across core processes.

Key Responsibilities

- Assist in the development and maintenance of Power BI dashboards and reports to support business and operational insights

- Support data preparation activities, including data cleaning, transformation, and validation using Power Query and SQL

- Help connect and integrate data from multiple sources, such as databases, spreadsheets, and business systems, into Power BI

- Create and maintain basic DAX measures and calculations under guidance from senior analysts

- Assist with data modeling tasks, including building and validating relationships and tables used for reporting

- Write SQL queries in Azure SQL Database to support reporting, data validation, and business analysis

- Help create and maintain automated workflows in Power Automate for notifications, approvals, and recurring business processes

- Support lightweight integrations and automation using Azure Functions where applicable

- Perform data quality checks and help identify data inconsistencies or anomalies

- Support documentation of report definitions, data sources, data models, business logic, and workflow steps

- Learn and follow BI best practices related to data governance, security, and reporting standards

Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related field

- Familiarity with Power BI, Power Query, and DAX

- Experience using Excel for data analysis, such as PivotTables, formulas, charts, lookups, and basic dashboards

- Power Automate skills, such as flows, connectors, approvals, scheduled and event-based triggers, conditions, loops, integrations, and error handling

- Azure SQL Database skills, such as writing queries, working with tables and views, joins, aggregations, stored procedures, triggers, and query optimization

- Azure Data Factory skills, such as linked services, datasets, copy activities, pipeline development, triggers, parameterization, monitoring, and error handling

- Azure Functions skills, such as Function Apps, triggers, bindings, service integrations, logging, troubleshooting, and serverless design

- Familiarity with databases, data warehouses, or ETL concepts from classes, projects, or internships

- Interest in building scalable, reliable data solutions that support better business decisions

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship.
